components.gap: The source's further claims about this same chain model on p. 106 (sec. 3.1, inside the body line-9 locator 'secs. 3.1-3.2.3, pp. 103-112') are treated nowhere on the handbook route. Pearl illustrates d-separation on the chain of Fig. 2(a) with its disturbance vertices: the path U_Z -> Z -> X -> Y is blocked by {Z} and by {X}, so the printed independencies 'U_X _||_ Y | Z' (the stated path yields U_Z _||_ Y | Z; the printed form fails in general) and U_Z _||_ Y | X hold in every probability function the model generates, whatever the parametrization; the collider path U_Z -> Z -> X <- U_X is blocked by the empty set but not by {Y}, so U_Z _||_ U_X holds while U_Z _||_ U_X | Y may fail. He names this handling of colliders Berkson's paradox (Berkson 1946), with the example of two independent coins made dependent by testimony that at least one is a tail, and claims that the d-separation independencies are the main opening through which structural-model assumptions confront nonexperimental data, almost all tests capable of invalidating the model being entailed by them, with note 7 (dormant independence, Shpitser and Pearl 2008, from some graphs with correlated errors). Body 922-923 says only that the source reads such implications off the diagram with d-separation; thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-chain-testable gives only the endogenous Z _||_ Y | X. Pearl's Definition 1 itself is on route as def:p16-active-path, and a coin-type collider calculation appears as thm:p16-collider-numerical-example (graphical-separation-adjustment.tex 264-297), but neither states these claims about the chain, the Berkson attribution, the testing claim or note 7.

components.gap: Lauritzen's Definition 2.47 (p. 66, inside the locator 'Propositions 2.46-2.48' of body lines 6-8, whose shared numbering spans Definition 2.47, and inside pp. 65-68) defines the Bayesian network (D,P) generated by D and the adapted kernels as their recursive combination P. components.gap: Theorem 1.28's proof (pp. 19-20) carries the source's justification for its construction: quantile functions are not unique, and although each is increasing and hence measurable, the various choices may destroy joint measurability, so the key is to remove the choices with an operationally defined quantile that singles out the largest p-quantile. The handbook proof (annex 199-244) adopts 'the source's upper quantile' and proves joint measurability, but nowhere states that separate quantile choices for different parameter values can fail to be jointly measurable, the reason the operational choice is needed. (The converse relation to the equations-to-kernels direction is reported at annex 314-316.)
components.basis: Jointly measurable rational upper quantile, CDF identification, Borel-image repair, the whole-model induction (independence of U_v from the constructed predecessors, conditional law, joint law equal to P_K) and the non-uniqueness example are written out.
Ordered, local and global properties as in the source's (O), (L), (G), with d-separation and its stated equivalence to ancestral moral separation.

components.gap: Lauritzen introduces Theorem 2.44 with the claim (p. 65) that, in contrast to the undirected case, the directed global, local and ordered Markov properties are all equivalent without further regularity assumptions. The handbook states the absence of regularity hypotheses (body 125-126, 209-211; no intersection axiom, positivity or density) but nowhere states the contrast with undirected graphs, whose corresponding properties need further assumptions; no undirected Markov property appears on the route. Also unreported is the p. 68 statement, on the cited page range, that when such a network has a density with respect to a product measure 'the results above can be strengthened'; body 5-8 says only that the source treats densities separately.

duties.duty: ED26-P16-CH-measurable-causal-graphs-C002 (partial): The status is proved=annex:p16.measurable-ci-calculus, but the full proof is missing for the clause 'Measurable functions may be applied to either independent tuple, also using the conditioning tuple as an argument' (body measurable-causal-graphs.tex 47-48). Its only argument is a one-clause sketch at annex 53-56: 'by pushing forward the conditional product kernels at each z'. Nothing shows that the regular conditional law of (g(X,Z),h(Y,Z)) given Z=z is the image of the conditional product law at z. The substitution identity of thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure that would give this is neither used nor cited, and the proof never returns from that identity to the product-test definition. The Z-free case, both equivalences and the four semigraphoid properties are fully argued.
duties.basis: Annex 55-146 now chooses the joint kernel pi, uses the single null set from the second equivalence, builds rho as the image under psi_z and identifies it with the regular conditional law of (g(X,Z),h(Y,Z)) by thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure (cited at 88 and 123), shows the product form off N, and returns to the product-test definition.

duties.duty: ED26-P16-CH-measurable-causal-graphs-C005 (partial): The status is proved=annex:p16.measurable-kernel-randomization, but the full proof is missing for the 'Consequently' assertion (body 90-94): every finite standard Borel kernel model has a representation X_v=F_v(X_pa(v),U_v) with mutually independent uniform U_v. Annex 157-160 says only 'Topological evaluation and successive conditioning show that its joint law is the kernel law'. It does not show that U_v is independent of the predecessors already constructed, that K_v(X_pa(v),.) is therefore their conditional law, or that induction identifies the joint law with P_K. The matching argument later at annex 508-513 is not invoked. The single-kernel realization (112-155) and the non-uniqueness example (160-166) are complete.
duties.basis: Annex 246-318 proves by induction that U_{v_k} is independent of the constructed predecessors, that K_{v_k}(X_pa,.) is their regular conditional law, and that the prefix laws equal the construction stages, ending with law P_K.

duties.duty: ED26-P16-CH-measurable-causal-graphs-C010 (partial): The status is proved=annex:p16.measurable-response-component, but the full proof is missing for the stated consequence (body 304-307): one conditional product law of (R,B) given C licenses integration of the whole family at a measurable random parameter depending on (B,C). Annex 567-573 is a two-sentence sketch. It does not derive L(R|B,C)=L(R|C) as kernels from R independent of B given C, and it does not substitute the random parameter into F via thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure. Separately, annex 537-538 ('by the separation hypothesis') relies, without stating or citing them, on two facts: exposing private roots preserves d-separation (stated only later, at 580-581) and the moral-separation bridge. The pointwise representation and R independent of B given C are argued (545-565).
duties.basis: Body 333-354 states the consequence precisely; annex 929-991 derives L(R|B,C) = L(R|C) as kernels from the first equivalence and integrates at theta(B,C) through thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure and tower; annex 870-874 cites the root-exposure lemma (body 304-316, annex 834-860) and the bridge.

duties.duty: ED26-P16-CH-measurable-causal-graphs-C012 (partial): The status is proved=annex:p16.measurable-mediation-fields, but the proof of item 1 (body 364-365) is incomplete. In the cross-world field, annex 610-611 claims 'The mediator tuple in this auxiliary model is exactly M_b, by topological evaluation on its restored ancestors'. For that, every exposure child that is an ancestor of a mediator must lie outside D_Y; annex 607-608 gives exposure input a to every exposure child in D_Y. The listed 'exact graph facts' (594-605) put into D_M only the heads of restored edges and their parents. No step places the other exposure children among the mediator ancestors in D_M, so the construction of M_b, and with it R_0 independent of M_b given C, is not fully argued. The claim at 613-615 that every vertex needed for Y belongs to D_Y is likewise only asserted. Items 2 and 3 and the reference-mediator law are argued.
duties.basis: Fact 1 (annex 1026-1039) puts every exposure descendant that is a mediator ancestor in D_M; Facts 3, 5 and 6 (1062-1149) construct M_b and prove by induction over D_Y that every vertex needed for Y is in D_Y with exposure input a and mediator inputs m.
